SECTION 7.16 Limitation on Use
of Proceeds . Request any Loan or Letter of Credit, and the Parent Borrower shall not use, shall procure that its Subsidiaries shall
not use, and shall use its reasonable best efforts to procure that its or their respective directors, officers, employees and agents shall
not use, the proceeds of any Loan or Letter of Credit

findings.proposedIrEvidence: condition[1] represents branch (b) as an AND expression whose three operands are: (1) use for the purpose of funding/financing/facilitating any activities, business or transaction of or with any Sanctioned Person, or in any Sanctioned Country; (2) 'to the extent such activities, business or transaction would be prohibited by Sanctions'; and (3) 'if conducted by a Person organized in any jurisdiction...'. The compiler's own reason on operand (2) states that it 'does not adjudicate' whether the qualifier limits the whole of branch (b) or only the 'in any Sanctioned Country' limb.
findings.sourceEvidence: (b) for the purpose of funding, financing or facilitating any activities, business or transaction of or with any Sanctioned Person, or in any Sanctioned Country to the extent such activities, business or transaction would be prohibited by Sanctions if conducted by a Person organized in any jurisdiction governed by the laws of the United States, the United Kingdom or in a European Union member state in which the Parent Borrower or any of its Subsidiaries is organized from time to time
findings.verifierReasoning: The IR's AND structure places the 'to the extent...' and 'if conducted by...' qualifiers inside the same conjunction as the whole 'Sanctioned Person, or in any Sanctioned Country' predicate, which necessarily applies those qualifiers to the Sanctioned-Person limb as well as the Sanctioned-Country limb. On the source's natural reading, the qualifier attaches only to the immediately preceding 'in any Sanctioned Country' limb, leaving the 'of or with any Sanctioned Person' limb unconditional. A hypothetical transaction with a Sanctioned Person that would not be prohibited by Sanctions under the hypothetical-organized-person test would therefore be outside the prohibition under the IR but within the source's Sanctioned-Person limb. The IR thus silently selects one reading of an ambiguous (or, on the natural reading, misgrouped) provision, and it does so despite claiming not to adjudicate the ambiguity. This can change a compliance conclusion and is material.

findings.proposedIrEvidence: The single rule has entityScope: [] and no condition or description representing the Parent Borrower's 'shall procure that its Subsidiaries shall not use' obligation, the 'reasonable best efforts to procure' standard as to directors, officers, employees and agents, or the restriction concerning 'Request any Loan or Letter of Credit'. All three conditions are phrased solely as a bare prohibition on 'use of the proceeds of any Loan or Letter of Credit'.
findings.sourceEvidence: Request any Loan or Letter of Credit, and the Parent Borrower shall not use, shall procure that its Subsidiaries shall not use, and shall use its reasonable best efforts to procure that its or their respective directors, officers, employees and agents shall not use, the proceeds of any Loan or Letter of Credit
findings.verifierReasoning: The source does not impose a single undifferentiated use-of-proceeds prohibition. It imposes a direct prohibition on the Parent Borrower, a 'shall procure' duty as to its Subsidiaries, and a 'reasonable best efforts' duty as to directors, officers, employees and agents, and it also restricts the requesting of a Loan or Letter of Credit. These have different obliged persons and different breach standards. The IR's empty entity scope and blanket PROHIBITION representation would mislead a reviewer about who is bound and under what standard—for example, a subsidiary's prohibited use is a Parent Borrower covenant breach only through the 'shall procure' duty, while a director's use is governed by the best-efforts standard. This omission is material.
